runner.note: This is the normative corpus and nothing executes it. evals/fixtures/protocol-conformance.json names conformance/vibeproof/v1/exact-byte-vectors.json as its normative_owner and then runs conformance/protocol/vibeproof-v1-vectors.json instead, so the shadow prototype has been standing in for the normative suite since the eval registry was written. eval_suite_ids is empty because no registry entry names this directory.

cases.title: Reproduce the exact canonical bytes, Sig_structure and COSE_Sign1 signature for a claim and a receipt
cases.note: scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py reproduces these vectors in Python today, which is one subject. Two independent codecs have never agreed on them, because neither exists.

cases.title: Refuse every malformed and resource-exhausting decoder input
cases.note: Thirty-three cases. Nine state their input as hex and are decoded by scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py, which requires the canonical profile decoder to refuse each one with the exact decoder_signal the case declares, so a case cannot claim a malformation its bytes do not contain. The other eighteen state a mutation, a generator or a transaction state in prose and are not executable until an implementation reads them. expect_reason_code names the canonical-decode class only; the corpus spans ten registry reason codes in total - CLAIM_INVALID_CANONICAL_ENCODING, CLAIM_INVALID_SIGNATURE, CLAIM_CHAIN_FORK, CLAIM_SEQUENCE_UNEXPECTED, CLAIM_GAP_DECLARATION_REQUIRED, BATCH_ATOMIC_REJECT, REQUEST_MALFORMED, IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT, DEVICE_KEY_CONTINUITY_BROKEN and STATE_TRANSITION_NOT_PERMITTED - each resolving in packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json, which this manifest has named as the suite's reason authority since it was written and which none of the original twenty cases resolved against. PF-070 added a third shape: six cddl_hex cases whose bytes decode cleanly under the canonical profile and are refused by the CDDL rule they name. That class did not exist, which is why atomic-batch-result-v1 and claim-result-v1 sat in cddl_rules_unpinned with the words "in prose state rather than in bytes", and why partial batch acceptance was prohibited by three documents and admitted by two schemas.

cases.title: Match the ZIP-215 verdict on every Ed25519 divergence case
cases.note: Nine cases where ZIP-215 and the cofactorless group equation disagree. A verifier that follows the wrong one accepts or rejects a signature the rest of the network decides the other way, which is a chain fork produced by a library choice.

cases.title: Refuse a signature the ZIP-215 oracle rejects, rather than accepting it under cofactorless verification
cases.note: The recorded run of github.com/hdevalence/ed25519consensus v0.2.0 against the divergence corpus, with go crypto/ed25519 and OpenSSL as contrast. It is an oracle result and not a verifier test: it says what the correct answer is, and no implementation of ours has been asked the question.

cases.title: Accept every pre-fork claim and resolve an unforked lineage without quarantining anything
cases.note: The positive half. `validate_lineage_fork_and_rotation` in scripts/repository/validate_planning_artifacts.py resolves five lineages: a control that accepts four submissions, a refusal lineage that opens no case, and three forks whose claims at or below the fork generation stay accepted. Without the control and the refusal lineage a resolver that answered `quarantined` to every input would satisfy the negative case below, which is the failure mode a fork corpus invites.

cases.title: Quarantine every post-fork branch and refuse a device-key transition missing either authorization
cases.note: The negative half, spanning two vocabularies. Three of the four D-072 detection bases are exercised at claim level and the fourth by the checkpoint vectors; every branch of every fork is quarantined including the one that arrived first, which is D-072 rather than bookkeeping. The rotation vectors remove the outgoing key signature, the incoming key signature and the account authentication one at a time and each removal must be refused with DEVICE_KEY_CONTINUITY_BROKEN, so the rule cannot be satisfied by any single one of the three. expect_reason_code names the fork class only; the corpus also resolves CLAIM_SEQUENCE_UNEXPECTED, CLAIM_GAP_DECLARATION_REQUIRED and DEVICE_KEY_CONTINUITY_BROKEN against packages/schemas/reason-codes-v1.json.
